name: Djiboutian Skoudehkaris
description: Skoudehkaris, meat and rice cooked together with warming whole spices, is widely considered Djibouti's national dish, reflecting real Yemeni and wider Horn of Africa spice-trade influence.
steps_detailed: Deeply brown the onion, 10-12 minutes, until golden.
Add the chicken, cumin, and cinnamon, and brown 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

description: Fah-fah, a spiced beef soup, is a genuine Djiboutian comfort food shared with the wider Horn of Africa region, closely related to Somali soups.

name: Djiboutian Lahoh
description: Lahoh, a spongy, fermented flatbread similar to Somali canjeero and Ethiopian injera, is a Djiboutian breakfast staple, traditionally torn and dipped in oil or stew.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin batter.
Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop some tang.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until bubbles form.

name: Djiboutian Xalwo
description: Xalwo (halwa), a dense, glossy, cardamom-scented sweet, is a beloved Djiboutian treat shared with Somalia, traditionally made for celebrations.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornstarch with 0.75 cup water until smooth, then add the sugar and cardamom.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Stir in the butter until melted and shiny.
